items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The final file was never shown. It is only 1730 bytes yet holds a hand-written base-1e9 BigInt plus the #/* ... ''' ... // ''' trick, so the code is likely terse and probably uses short names in the BigInt and Fibonacci loops. The final message does explain the trick.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The structure is simple: C section first, then the Python section after #if 0. But the custom BigInt in C goes beyond what the task needed and adds code to maintain. The test files in /app were cleaned up afterwards.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Missing arguments give a non-zero exit in both modes ("Exited with non-zero"). Negative or non-numeric N was never tested. Python's int() would raise a traceback on bad input, and range(-1) would just print 0. The C side's bounds for BigInt sizing and input parsing are unverified.

items.name: Boundary and large inputs
items.evidence: Both versions are iterative, f(0)=0 and f(1)=1, and the outputs match up to N=10000, so C is exact beyond n=93 thanks to the BigInt. Missing args exit non-zero. Rejection of negative or non-numeric input was not shown in either language.

items.name: Exact invocation contract
items.evidence: The exact commands work: `gcc main.py.c -o cmain && cmain 10` -> 55, and `python3 main.py.c 10` -> 55. It compiles cleanly under -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic, and python -W error runs clean. Only the number is printed. Hidden tests pass.
